composed_config_diff.reading: every differing leaf is bookkeeping except the AGREE arm's committed supply pin, which the A/A drops (item E16) and which reaches a request only through the supply's output; proof 2 finds the outputs byte-identical to each other, to the registered digest and to the committed artifact, and proof 3 finds every request byte identical

hash_quoting: 64-hex identities other than the prepared-supply output digests and the study commit are quoted as sha256-prefix16:<first 16 hex> (core.flight.repin rewrites package JSON from old identity hashes to new ones at the flip and refuses any old hash left under docs/); the full values are recomputable from study_commit

agree_arm.source: the AGREE arm's committed artifact (the one that flew), read raw -- not re-minted

prepared_supply.note: the recorded INPUTS differ (the run id, and the implementation identity the W3 merge moved), which is why the committed artifact no longer loads at HEAD; output_sha256 is core.preparation.digest over the {facets, values} payload and is what the flip's byte-identity check and the request composer consume

question: Is the knowledge wave's shared in-chain A/A (SAEA-SLURP-STAGE3-WAVE1-AA-FOLD-A-V1) the retained AGREE arm's own bytes (SAEA-SLURP-STAGE3-AGREE-W1-FOLD-A-V1): byte-identical prepared first-phase supply output and byte-identical composed request bytes? If so, W1, W3 and W4 are each read at it (decision 164).

request_bytes.method: the decision-160 method verbatim (P160.capture_requests): FlightRuntime._dispatch_phase_program(model_free_check=True) on each cell's own composed fragments, against the composed model fragment's REAL llama-server transport with its POST replaced by a fake server that records the body bytes and answers a canned, role-appropriate completion; a fake session receipt bound to the fragment's decoder identity; keyed by (sample_id, contact_id); dispatched serially

scheduling_self_control.what: the wave A/A dispatched twice, both at the production concurrency (np4 geometry: four slots, queue depth 16), each under its own scratch run id; the number of contacts on which each field differs between the two dispatches of the SAME cell. These fields are assigned by arrival order (request_id, the rails-message/<request_id>/ provenance relpaths, the slot id) or derived from the run id (source_query_state_sha256), which is why the A/A comparison dispatches serially and reads the run-id-derived field separately
